meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 5 (Ind AS 115 — Revenue from Contracts with Customers).

questions.q: How many performance obligations does the contract contain?
questions.why: The customer can benefit from the handset and each service on its own (readily available separately), and the items are not inputs to one combined output; the services are not highly interdependent. Three distinct performance obligations.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Count distinct benefits, then test combination — bundling is the exception, not the rule. Distinct = stands alone. The plan is a gift basket, not one machine.

questions.stem: Teleco Ltd sells a plan for Rs 18,000 (24 months) comprising: (i) a handset delivered on day 1 (standalone price Rs 9,000), (ii) connectivity for 24 months (standalone Rs 9,000), (iii) cloud storage for 24 months (standalone Rs 6,000). Teleco recognises Rs 9,000 on handset delivery and the remaining Rs 9,000 evenly over the 24 months.

questions.q: Under Ind AS 115's default allocation, revenue for the handset is:
questions.why: Relative SSP: total SSP 24,000 (9,000+9,000+6,000); handset = 18,000 × 9/24 = Rs 6,750. The Rs 6,000 bundle discount is spread proportionately absent observable evidence tying it to one obligation.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: relative-SSP allocation is the case's core arithmetic Allocate by price-tags, not by who-does-what: each rupee of discount rides proportionately.

questions.q: The handset revenue of Rs 6,750 is recognised:
o: When the first bill is paid
Half at delivery, half at term end
questions.why: Control of the handset (a good) transfers on delivery; nothing in the contract integrates it with the services, so point-in-time recognition of the allocated amount.

questions.q: Compared with the correct treatment, Teleco's approach causes:
o: Over-recognition in year 1 by Rs 1,125 and a wrong profile, though totals agree over 24 months
questions.why: Correct year 1: 6,750 + 3,375 + 2,250 = 12,375; Teleco books 9,000 + 4,500 = 13,500 ⇒ Rs 1,125 too much early — a classic 'totals match, timing wrong' breach of allocation.

questions.q: In Ind AS 115's five-step model, transaction price is allocated to performance obligations:
o: On the basis of expected cost of each obligation
On a relative standalone selling price basis
By gross margin of each obligation
questions.why: Step 4 requires allocation based on relative standalone selling prices, with exceptions for discounts attributable to specific obligations and variable consideration allocated wholly/partially to a specified obligation where criteria are met.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the five-step skeleton underpins most revenue MCQs Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: 5 steps: Identify contract → Identify POs → Determine price → Allocate (relative SSP) → Recognise on fulfilment. Allocation speaks in STANDALONE prices, never costs.
mem.link: Ch 5

questions.q: A contract includes a performance bonus of Rs 10 crore. Management's most likely outcome is receipt, but the bonus will not be determined for 14 months. Ind AS 115 requires the entity to include the variable amount in the transaction price only to the extent it is:
o: Probable of not resulting in a significant revenue reversal later
questions.why: Variable consideration is constrained: include it only to the extent it is probable that a significant reversal will NOT occur when the uncertainty reverses. Long measurement periods and broad outcome ranges increase constraint.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — constraint questions test reading precision — near-identical options recur AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Constraint = no big revenue whipsaw. Include variable amounts only as far as 'probable no significant reversal' — the reversal, not the receipt, is the guardrail.
mem.link: Ch 5

questions.topic: Ind AS 115 — contract assets vs receivables
questions.q: A performance obligation is satisfied over time and revenue recognised exceeds amounts billed to date. The balance should be presented as:
questions.why: When fulfilment precedes billing, the right to consideration is CONDITIONAL on further performance ⇒ contract asset. A receivable is an UNCONDITIONAL right to consideration (only time needed).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the asset-vs-receivable cut-off is a staple Section B idea AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 115 — contract assets vs receivables
mem.tip: Contract asset = needs more work. Receivable = needs only time. Ask: what still stands between me and the cash?
mem.link: Ch 5

questions.q: A manufacturer offers a legally required basic warranty for two years plus an extended warranty sold separately. Under Ind AS 115:
o: Both are accounted for under Ind AS 37 provisions
The basic warranty is an assurance-type warranty under Ind AS 37; the extended warranty is a service-type warranty = a separate performance obligation
The basic warranty is a performance obligation; extended is a provision
questions.why: Assurance-type warranties (quality promise, legally required or customary) ⇒ provision under Ind AS 37. Service-type warranties (sellable separately, beyond the assurance) ⇒ additional performance obligation with revenue deferred over its period.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — assurance-vs-service classification repeats across attempts AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Two warranties, two books: assurance→provision; service→revenue. Can it be bought alone? Then it's a service.
mem.link: Ch 5 + Ch 7

questions.q: An online marketplace collects Rs 500 crore of customer payments for third-party sellers, keeps a 10% commission, and sets neither inventory price nor product specifications. Revenue recognition is:
o: Gross with cost of services matched
Net only if the marketplace has inventory risk
questions.why: Control of the specified good/service before transfer determines principal status. No inventory risk, no price discretion, no specification control ⇒ agent ⇒ net commission revenue.
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — principal-vs-agent with gross/net maths is an ICAI perennial AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 115 — principal vs agent
mem.tip: Principal controls before transfer; agent merely arranges. No inventory risk, no pricing power ⇒ show only the commission.
mem.link: Ch 5 + Ch 11

questions.q: A customer prepays a full year's subscription in advance; the advance financing the entity is incidental. Ind AS 115 requires the entity to:
o: Adjust the transaction price for the time value of money in all cases
Not adjust where the payment timing does not provide a significant benefit of financing (practical expedient: ≤1 year also simplifies)
questions.why: SFCs adjust the transaction price for the time value of money unless the timing gap (≤12-month practical expedient) or the purpose is non-financing. Prepayment within a year — no adjustment.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 12-month practical expedient is the exact MCQ hook AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.ti: TI: Ind AS 115 — significant financing component
mem.tip: 12-month rule: short gaps, no interest games. Financing significant only when the delay IS the deal.
mem.link: Ch 5

questions.q: A licence of IP that the entity has no ongoing obligation to update and the customer can use immediately after grant results in revenue:
o: At the point in time when the licence is transferred (right to use)
In proportion to future marketing spend
questions.why: Right-to-USE licences → point-in-time on transfer/start of period. Right-to-ACCESS (entity's ongoing activities affect the IP) → over time. Royalties on IP: recognize as sales occur.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — use-vs-access phrasing decides the answer AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: 'Use it now, we won't touch it' → point in time. 'We keep it alive; you ride our updates' → over time.
mem.link: Ch 5

questions.q: Two contracts entered into at or near the same time with the same counterparty are accounted for as ONE when:
o: They are signed by the same officer
They are negotiated as a package with a single commercial objective, consideration in one depends on the other, or they form a single PO
questions.why: Ind AS 115 combination criteria: single commercial objective/package, interdependent consideration, or combined performance obligation.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the three-limb test is quoted verbatim in objective papers Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Three fuses: one objective, linked payments, or one obligation — any one glues the contracts together.

questions.q: Non-cash consideration in the transaction price is measured at:
o: Carrying amount in the customer's books
questions.why: Ind AS 115: measure non-cash consideration at fair value at (or near) contract inception; if FV can't be measured reliably, use the standalone selling price of the goods/services promised.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — measurement-at-inception quirks test reading speed Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Valued at inception, not delivery; if unvaluable, borrow the SSP of what you handed over.

questions.q: A contract modification is accounted for as a SEPARATE contract when:
o: Additional goods are priced at their standalone selling prices reflecting the new circumstances
The client agrees to pay more
questions.why: Ind AS 115: separate contract if the scope increases with consideration equal to standalone prices for the additional goods/services — no reallocation of prior revenue.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — the three-modification routes is the exam's spine Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: 'Fair price for extra scope' = new deal; otherwise adjust — re-separate or catch-up.

questions.q: Consideration paid to a customer is treated as:
o: A reduction of the transaction price unless for a distinct good/service received at fair value
questions.why: 115 treats customer payments as price concessions, unless they buy distinct goods/services — then measure the purchase separately at FV (excess to P&L as expense if paid > FV of the good).
questions.trend: Core concept that appears in some avatar in most attempts under the new scheme (pattern estimate).

mem.tip: If you pay for nothing distinct, you effectively discounted your own price.

questions.q: Costs to obtain a contract are capitalised under Ind AS 115 when:
o: They are incremental to winning the contract AND expected to be recovered
questions.why: Incremental costs of obtaining (e.g., sales commission) are recognised as an asset if expected to be recovered; amortised consistent with the related goods/services transfer.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).

questions.q: Kaveri Ltd sells a bundled contract (services P, Q, R) for Rs 213 lakh. Standalone selling prices: P Rs 90 lakh, Q Rs 110 lakh, R Rs 50 lakh. Ind AS 115 allocates the price as:
o: Service P: Rs 76.7 lakh; Q: Rs 93.7 lakh; R: Rs 42.6 lakh
questions.why: Relative SSP allocation: total SSP 250; P = 213 × 90/250 = 76.7 lakh; Q = 93.7; R = 42.6. Cost-based or equal splits are not the default; the bundle discount is spread proportionately absent specific evidence.
questions.trend: Repeated theme in recent ICAI exam question-patterns for this paper (AI pattern estimate — not a citation to a specific past paper question).
questions.probWhy: HIGH likelihood for Nov 2026 — relative-SSP allocation sums are the revenue chapter's favourite calculation Prediction is study guidance, not an ICAI statement.

mem.tip: Allocate on relative standalone selling prices; a bundle discount follows the SSPs unless attributable evidence exists.
